newsitem.title: USA: U.S.-North Korea missile talks re-set for June.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-North Korea missile talks re-set for June.

text.p: U.S.-North Korean talks aimed at getting Pyongyang to halt its missile sales, postponed by North Korea earlier this month, have been rescheduled for mid-June, the State Department said Tuesday.
Spokesman John Dinger said the talks would be held in New York June 11-13.
The talks were to have been held in New York May 12-13, but Pyongyang postponed them for what it called "technical reasons".
Dinger said the talks would be led for the United States by deputy assistant secretary of state Robert Einhorn and for North Korea by foreign ministry director Li Hyong-chol.
"We will address North Korea's missile proliferation activities, which are of great concern," he said.
The United States has made clear its concern over Pyongyang's missile sales to Iran and Syria and has said progress on this issue is crucial to improved U.S.-North Korean ties.
